assumptions: A property of the executable on a declared-synthetic fixture, established by enumeration over P(K). It is not a proof about an unbounded rule language, and it re-runs per fixture rather than holding once.
Monotonicity of each T_e gives order-independence of the chaotic iteration. It does not make any individual narrowing TRUE — that is a per-edge proof obligation nobody has met.
attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s P1 against INV-R7.4, adopted whole and then generalised. R7.4 checked monotonicity by comparing AUTHORED RULES to each other — `rule A.when ⊆ rule B.when ⇒ check A.then ⊆ B.then` — which omits the executable’s fall-through: an input matching no rule goes to ⊤, and those points are part of T. Adding `{authority, provenance} → ∅` to E6 makes the actual function non-monotone ({authority} ⊆ {authority,provenance} while T = ⊤ ⊄ ∅) and R7.4’s gate printed `✓ every declared rule set is MONOTONE` and exited 0. Registered as M5 and required to go red. THE REPAIR IS ENUMERATION, NOT A BETTER INSPECTION: |P(K)| = 2^5 = 32, so all 32 inputs and all 243 comparable pairs are evaluated per edge on transfer() itself. WHAT MONOTONICITY IS FOR, executed rather than asserted: a six-edge graph whose Y-label grows by two paths of different length, with a non-monotone T on the last edge, returns THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS over its 720 edge orderings — and 302 of them return ∅, the closure reporting NOTHING AFFECTED. The same graph with a monotone T returns one answer in all 720. R7.4 stated this consequence in a justification string and never ran it.

coverage.domain: every edge in mosaic/embodiment.json impact_algebra.graph × every ordered pair (A,B) with A ⊆ B drawn from P(kinds) for the kinds registered at this schema revision — 9 edges × 243 comparable pairs

attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, on ROUND7_4_MOSAIC_BRIEF.md §4. Ordinary abstract interpretation: a monotone transfer over a finite lattice gives a least fixpoint reachable by chaotic iteration in any order. SRC-DENNING-1976-LATTICE for the carrier.

attrs.review_focus: The general lesson is a hierarchy, not a rule about monotonicity: FINITE + CHEAP → exhaustive extensional comparison; DECIDABLE but larger → property-based search; TOO LARGE → mutation-derived distinguishing controls. R7.4 was arguing about which control to hand-pick in a domain with 32 elements.
attrs.statement: For every edge, the TOTAL transfer function transfer(edge, ·) : P(K) → P(K) — including every input that matches no declared rule — is monotone: A ⊆ B implies T(A) ⊆ T(B).
